rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wave separated Noah from his son, or the son from the mountain, and the son was among those drowned because he had not boarded with Noah.
rows.anchor: أي بين الابن والجبل أو بينه وبين أبيه

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says father and son were still exchanging words when a great wave suddenly swallowed the son and his horse, cutting him off from Noah.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : قل كانا يتراجعان الكلام فما استتمت لمراجعة حتى جاءت موجة عظيمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage defines riding as mounting or being above something, running as passing swiftly or unobstructed, and a wave as a great raised mass of water.
rows.anchor: والركوب : العلو على ظهر الشيء , ركب الدابة والسفينة والبر والبحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mountain is a massive upright body rooted in earth, while protection means prevention from harm.
rows.anchor: والجبل : جسم عظيم الغلظ شاخص من الأرض هو لها كالوتد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth is told to swallow the flood gradually and secretly, with its scope limited to the water made to drown people, as though it were nourishment for the earth.
rows.anchor: { يا أرض ابلعي } اي اجذبي من غير مضغ إلى مكان خفي بالتدريج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sky is ordered to stop raining; both earth and sky promptly obey the sovereign whose will nothing escapes.
rows.anchor: { ويا سماء أقلعي } اي أمسكي عن الإمطار , ففعلتا مبادرتين لأمر الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water receded into the earth; the passive form of the command highlights the actor's majesty, since no one else can perform these acts.
rows.anchor: { وغيض الماء } اي المعهود , حكم عليه بالدبوب في أعماق الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The decree was fully accomplished, with the destruction of those who perished and rescue of those saved exactly as promised Noah; no one could delay it.
rows.anchor: في إهلاك نم هلك ونجاة من نجا كما أراد الجليل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada dates the Ark's departure to the tenth of Rajab, its time afloat to 150 days, its stay at al-Judi to a month, and disembarkation to Ashura.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : استقلت بهم لعشر خلون من رجب وكانت في الماء خمسين وماءئة يوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Judi's name intimates that universal vengeance has passed and generosity, water, fertility, and mercy remain; the mountain is near Mosul.
rows.anchor: وما بقي إلا الجود بالماء والخير والخصب والرحمة العامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The curse of distance became a conventional curse of destruction; its use as a verbal noun marks the unjust people as deserving it.
rows.anchor: ثم استعير للهلاك وخص بدعاء السوء

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan counts twenty-one rhetorical devices in the nineteen-word verse and reports that a Bedouin called it the speech of the powerful.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية تسع عشرة لفظة فيها أحدوعشرون نوعا من البديع - عدها أبو حيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disagreement among Moses' people and others was culpable disbelief, and the disputants remain in deep doubt about the judgment or the Scripture despite the signs they witnessed.
rows.anchor: ولما كانا لاختلاف قد يكون بغير الكفر بين أنه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that God will repay all their deeds is certain; the fronted phrase stresses that he knows every deed and omits none.
rows.anchor: لا يخفى عليه منها شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the lightened reading of لما, the particle is an emphatic lām plus mā, affirming the statement by denying its opposite.
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة غيرهم بالتخفيف مركبة من لام الابتداء و { ما } المؤكدة بنفي نقيض

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Hajib says deleting the verb after jussive لما is common and eloquent; the implied verb here is that God will judge between them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن احلاجب : وهو شائع فصيح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the doubled reading, the author treats إن as emphatic and لما as a jussive particle whose omitted verb is supplied by the context.
rows.anchor: في قراءة ابن عامر وحمزة وعاصم بالتشديد الجازمة حذف فعلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet must exert himself to stand firm as commanded, in personal conduct and conveying the message, following earlier prophets in roots and branches, without being unsettled by mockery or demands to conceal revelation.
rows.anchor: بغاية جهدك بسبب أنك لا تلكف إلا نفسك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who repented from disbelief must also remain upright with the Prophet and not become anxious about delayed help.
rows.anchor: ولما كان الفاصل بين المعطوف والمعطوف عليه يقوم مقام تأكيد الضمير المستتر

rows.speaker: خباب بن الأرت
rows.claim: Khabbab reports that the Prophet recalled believers tortured by sawing and iron combs who stayed faithful, then promised Islam's completion and safe travel from Sana'a to Hadramawt; he told his impatient hearers they were hasty.
rows.anchor: كما روى البخاري وابو داود والنسائي عن خباب بن الأرت رضي الله عنه قال : شكونا إلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says no verse was harder or more burdensome for the Prophet than this one.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : ما نزلت على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم آية اشد ولا أشق من هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Uprightness means continuing along one course; the command is moderate between excess and neglect, and people rarely escape neglect, which can humble them, while excess breeds pride and can make someone act as a lawgiver.
rows.anchor: والاستقامة : الاستمرار في جهة واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not exceed the limits of commands or prohibitions: religion is moderate, intended to discipline people rather than meet God's need, and modest practice with sound purpose is sufficient.
rows.anchor: { ولا تطغوا } أي تتجاوزوا الحد فيما أمرتم به أو نهيتم عنه بالزيادة إفراطا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition of excess also implies, a fortiori, a prohibition of falling short; alternatively, it warns against letting prosperity make one arrogant or deviate from the straight path.
rows.anchor: ولما نهى عن الإفراط وهو الزيادة تصريحا , فأفهم النهي عن التفريط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root of طغى revolves around exceeding a limit while rising; the author connects its derivatives to covering, night, flood, sea, disobedience, fertile lowlands, and Syria's well-watered Ghuta.
rows.anchor: ومادة ( طغى ) واوية ويائية بكل ترتيب تدور على مجاوزة الحد مع العلو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After forbidding excess, the passage forbids falling short and warns against leaning even slightly toward wrongdoers; love and hatred for God are faith's strongest bonds, while attachment to wrongdoers binds one to Satan.
rows.anchor: ولما نهي عن الإفراط في الدين , أتبعه النهي عن التفريط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaning toward those who have done wrong includes inclining to their conduct, approving or imitating them, and adopting their style; the paired commands mean neither wrong yourself nor admire wrongdoers' deeds.
rows.anchor: أي بالميل إليهم بأن تثاقل أنفسكم نحوهم للميل إلى أعمالهم ولو بالرضى به والتشبه بهم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari interprets ركون as a slight inclination; the author likes its meaning but says he found no other linguist supporting it.
rows.anchor: وفسر الزمخشري الركون بالميل اليسير , وهو حسن من جهة المعنى

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani's definition is closer: ركون is settling toward something with affection and inclination, opposite to aversion.
rows.anchor: وقال الرماني - وهو أقرب : الركون : السكون إلى الشيء بالمحبة والانصباب إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This warning echoes 11:12; leaning toward wrongdoers brings the touch of the Fire, from which people cannot free themselves by any stratagem.
rows.anchor: والآية ملتفتة إلى قوله تعالى { فلعلك تارك بعض ما يوحى إليك }

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan observes that the Prophet is addressed alone in commands to good deeds but the community is addressed collectively in prohibitions of evil.
rows.anchor: ومن إجلال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إفراده بالخطاب في الأمر بأفعال الخير , والإتيان بضمير الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No ally short of God can rescue them from his punishment; the wording portrays such rescue as impossible and far away.
rows.anchor: وأعرق في النفي فقال : { من أولياء } أي يخلصونكم من عذابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is the highest expiation for the weakness and lassitude that cause minor sins, and after faith it is the best act of worship and the broadest aid to uprightness.
rows.anchor: وذلك يدل على أنها بعد الإيمان أفضل العبادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two ends of the day mean morning and afternoon prayers, as prescribed in Mecca before the Night Journey; noon may also be intended as the second end.
rows.anchor: بالصبح والعصر كما كان مفروضا بمكة في أول الأمر قبل الإسراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zulaf are groups, stages, or periods of night; they may mean the early obligatory night vigil, or Maghrib and Isha with witr or night vigil.
rows.anchor: يمكن أن يكون المراد به التهجد , فقد كان مفروضا في أول الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All acts of obedience grounded in faith, including prayer, erase minor sins; major sins require repentance, while merely avoiding them expiates only with a sound intention.
rows.anchor: الطاعات كلها الصلاة وغيرها المبنية على أساس الإيمان

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that after a man confessed to kissing a woman, the Prophet recited this verse and said it applies to whoever among his community acts by it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه أم رجلا أصاب من امرأة قبلة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas regards the verse as belonging to the Meccan and Medinan portions of the surah; the cited report supports that view.
rows.anchor: وهذا الحديث يؤيد قول ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : إن هذه الآية من هذه السورة المكية المدنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding exhortation, warning, consolation, and instruction in the remedy for misery form a great reminder for those able to attend, reflect clearly, and understand deeply.
rows.anchor: الأمر العالي الرتبة الذي تقدم من الترغيب والترهيب والتسلية وتعليم الداء والدواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Be patient in obedience, away from sin, and in continuing to warn; do not fear opponents, since the outcome favors those who obey.
rows.anchor: { واصبر } أي ليكن منك صبر على الطاعات وعن المعاصي ولا تترك إنذارهم بما أمرت به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God never wastes the reward of people perfected in worshipful excellence; patience is difficult, but obedience requires it, and religion as a whole is patience.
rows.anchor: الصبر هو الإحسان كل الإحسان وإن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the report that Paradise is surrounded by hardships and Hell by desires, and links the promise to the verse that the patient receive their reward without measure.
rows.anchor: فلادين كله صبر ( حفت الجنة بالمكاره والنار بالشهوات ) ولذا فضل ثواب الصابر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women say the governor's wife's passion is plain and intense; their quick report to her implies they wanted her to react, which the author calls their plot.
rows.anchor: وكأنهن أردن بهذا الكلام أن يتأثر عنه ما فعلت امرأة العزيز ليرنيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife prepared soft couches and luxurious cushions, then gave each woman a knife for cutting the food served at the gathering.
rows.anchor: ما يتكئن عليه من الفرش اللينة والوسائد الفاخرة

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan reports that the food may have been meat, which people cut with knives instead of biting, while al-Rummani says it was fruit.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : فقيل : كان لحما

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani says the women were given knives to cut fruit; the author adds that the deeper purpose was to make them experience the same attraction and excuse the wife.
rows.anchor: وقال الرماني : ليقطعن فاكهة قدمت إليهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated verb for cutting suggests many wounds: each woman reflexively lifted the knife after a cut, then her absorption led to further cuts; their blame became an excuse.
rows.anchor: فكأن السكين كانت تقع على يد إحداهن فتجرحها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women glorify God because Joseph's beauty exceeds ordinary humanity; his restraint was not caused by weakness, and the culture associates surpassing beauty and chastity with angels.
rows.anchor: { ما هذا بشرا } لأنه فاق الشر في الحسن جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wife admits that she seduced Joseph and that he resisted, then threatens imprisonment if he disobeys; the threat is meant to shame and separate him from her.
rows.anchor: { راودته عن نفسه } أي لأصل إليه بما أريد { فاستعصم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavy emphatic nūn strengthens the threat of imprisonment, while the lighter nūn marks the threat of humiliation; alternatively, prison receives stronger emphasis because it separates the beloved.
rows.anchor: أكدتهع بالنون الثقيلة وقالت : { وليكونا } بالنون الخفيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph addresses God without a request particle, absorbed in witnessing God, and defends himself against the combined temptations of beauty, rank, wealth, and the women's persuasion.
rows.anchor: دافعا عن نفسه ما ورد عليه من وسوسة الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling prison more beloved is deliberately paradoxical: Joseph dislikes both options, but says imprisonment is the lesser evil and the women's invitation is more abhorrent.
rows.anchor: { أحب إلي } أي أقل بغضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison itself proves the intended meaning: nobody normally loves prison, so the expression of love makes clear that he would prefer it to the worse alternative.
rows.anchor: ومع ذلك فأنا أوثره على ما ندعونني إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dua is a request addressed upward to one above the speaker, though its form resembles a command addressed downward to a subordinate.
rows.anchor: وصيغته كصيغة الأمر إلا أن الدعاء لمن فوقك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If God does not repel their scheme, Joseph may incline toward them because people are naturally susceptible; once chastity is breached, further transgressions follow, and he would become deeply ignorant.
rows.anchor: أي ما قد التبس من مكرهن وتدبيرهن الذي يردن به الخبث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answered Joseph and repelled the women's scheme, fulfilling the prior promise that God would turn evil away from him.
rows.anchor: { كذلك لتصرف عنه السوء } [ يوسف : 24 ] للآية { فصرف عنه كيدهن }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the Hearer of spoken words and Knower of hidden intentions, answering when purpose is sincere and resolve is pure.
rows.anchor: فيجيب ما صح فيه القصد وطاب منه العزم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The quoted poetic maxim says that praise can suffice instead of an explicit request, illustrating how generosity responds to an allusion.
rows.anchor: إذا أثنى عليك المرء يوما … كفاه من تعرضه الثناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the evidence should have kept Joseph from prison, God made imprisonment a means of frustrating the women's plot and establishing his rank, displaying divine power by overturning ordinary expectations.
rows.anchor: كان حينئذ أبعد شيء عن السجن لو كان الناس متمكنين من جري أمورهم على حسب السديد من عقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rulers knowingly chose an unjust and foolish imprisonment as part of God's overriding plan, which repeatedly overturns customary causes.
rows.anchor: ففعلوا - مع علمهم بأن ذلك ظلم وسفه - إجابة لغالب أمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bada means something appeared after being hidden and a change of opinion as a new consideration emerged; they decided to imprison him until the gossip faded.
rows.anchor: التلون فيه لظهور ما لم يكن ظهر منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view says the period was seven years; another account says the wife told the governor that Joseph had disgraced her and asked either to leave and apologize or to join him in prison.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن ذلك الحين سبع سنين , قيل : كان سبب ذلك أنها قالت للعزيز : إن هذا قد فضحني

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Joseph was paraded on a donkey with a drum beaten before him, while callers in Egypt's markets announced his alleged crime and sentence.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : فأمر به فحمل على حمار وضرب أمامه بالطبل

rows.speaker: أبو صالح
rows.claim: Abu Salih says Ibn Abbas wept whenever he related the story of Joseph's public humiliation.
rows.anchor: قال أبو صالح : ما ذكر ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما هذا الحديث إلا بكى

rows.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says every stage in Joseph's story combined gentleness with hardship, blessing with trial, and eventual relief; harsh coercion can lead to the best outcome with fewer consequences.
rows.anchor: قال الإمام فخر الدين الرازي في كتاب اللوامع : وعلى الجملة فكل أحوال يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prison that appeared to humiliate Joseph instead became a source of honor and showed God's control of events while fulfilling his prior promise.
rows.anchor: وكان سببا ظاهرا في الإهانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two young inmates were the king's baker and cupbearer; the baker suspected that the cupbearer had helped him poison the king.
rows.anchor: فتيان } : خباز الملك وساقيه , ورفع إليه أن الخباز أراد أن يسمه

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says the word مع indicates companionship beginning at that point, so all three entered prison at the same time.
rows.anchor: تدل على الصحبة واستحداثها , فهي تدل على دخول الثلاثة السجن في آن واحد - قاله أبو حيانز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph cared for fellow prisoners by comforting the grieving, visiting the sick, advocating for the poor, guiding people to good, and reminding them of God; they felt spiritually blessed by his company.
rows.anchor: يسلي حزينهم , ويعود مريضهم , ويسأل لفقيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prisoners and guard praised Joseph's face, character, and speech, and valued the reward, expiation, and purity they learned from him; the guard wished he could release him.
rows.anchor: ما أحسن وجهك وأحسن خلقك وأحسن حديثك ! لقد بورك لنا في جوارك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asked the two young men not to love him, explaining that love from his aunt, father, and his companion's wife had each preceded a new affliction; they loved him anyway.
rows.anchor: فوالله ما أحبني أحد قط إلا دخل علي من جهته بلاء

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi suggests the inmates may have invented the dreams to test Joseph, or perhaps they had seen nothing at all.
rows.anchor: كما قال الشعبي - وإنما صنفا هذا ليختبراه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their first dream describes a past scene: pressing means extracting liquid, and wine here means grapes destined to become wine.
rows.anchor: والعصر : الاعتماد على ما فيه مائية ليحتلب منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Carrying is lifting an object with support for transport; bread is prepared food, and birds eating from it completes the second dream.
rows.anchor: أي طعاما مهيأ للأكل بالخبز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inmates ask for interpretation, meaning the outcome to which the dream leads; they infer Joseph can interpret because they see him as excellent in all his affairs.
rows.anchor: أي ما يرجع أمره ويصير إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph seizes their receptiveness to give the most important counsel first: sincere worship of God and rejection of associationism, before answering the dream.
rows.anchor: وهو ما خلق العباد له من الاجتماع على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars should give essential counsel when asked a question and may describe their knowledge to help listeners accept it, provided this guides them toward God rather than self-praise.
rows.anchor: فعلى كل ذي علم إذا احتاج إلى سؤاله أحد أن يقدم على جوابه نصحه بما هو الأهم له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph promises to interpret any food they receive while awake before it arrives, including what it is and what it will lead to.
rows.anchor: وبين أنه خاص بهما دون أهل السجن بقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His knowledge is a portion granted by his Lord, the one who created, nurtured, and treated him well; it is neither divination nor astrology.
rows.anchor: أي الموجد لي والمربي لي والمحسن إلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling them prison companions evokes shared hardship, which removes worldly pretension and softens the heart toward friendship.
rows.anchor: أي الذي تزول فيه الحظوظ ويحصل الانكسار للنفس والرقة في القلب فتتخلص فيه المودة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph leaves the identity of the condemned prisoner ambiguous, allowing each man to hope he is the one restored unless they demand a specific answer.
rows.anchor: فإن ألجأه إلى التعيين كان ذلك عذرا له في الخروج عن الأليق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cupbearer will serve wine to his master again; the baker will be crucified by the king and birds will eat from his head.
rows.anchor: وهو الساقي فيلخص ويقرب { فيسقي ربه } أي سيده الذي في خدمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive verb for crucifixion reflects that only the king has authority to crucify; the paired clauses use ellipsis, with each outcome implying its opposite counterpart.
rows.anchor: بنى للمفعول قوله : { فيصلب } ويعطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the two men denied seeing anything and said they were playing, but Joseph insists their case is settled and his interpretation is neither ignorance nor error.
rows.anchor: وروى أنهما قالا : ما رأينا شيئا , إنما كنا نلعب

rows.speaker: الرماني
rows.claim: Al-Rummani distinguishes fatwa as an answer about a matter's meaning from an answer that gives its underlying cause.
rows.anchor: الجواب بحكم المعنى , وهو غير الجواب بعلته - ذكره الرماني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dreams may foreshadow the king's: pressed grapes signify green ears and fat cattle, while the birds eating the baker's bread signify dry ears and lean cattle.
rows.anchor: فالعصير يشير إلى السنابل الخضر والبقر السمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ظن may mean knowledge, since all human knowledge is nothing beside God's, or ordinary inference from clues; this could permit decisive speech based on probability, or the subject may be the cupbearer.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون الظن على بابه لكونه قال ما مضى اجتهادا بقرائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph asks the cupbearer to tell the king about Joseph's virtue and clean character, which contradict the accusation against him; رب here means the king, unlike God's use elsewhere.
rows.anchor: أي سيدك ملك مصر , بما رأيت مني من معالي الأخلاق وطهارة الشيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author distinguishes the human master called رب in Joseph's request from the divine Lord in his earlier contrast of separate lords.
rows.anchor: أرباب متفرقون } ) 77 [ يوسف : 39 ] . فنجا الساقي وصلب صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As Joseph predicted, the cupbearer survived and the baker was crucified; Satan made the cupbearer forget Joseph because Joseph relied on him, prolonging Joseph's imprisonment.
rows.anchor: أي الساقي { الشيطان } أي البعيد من الرحمة المحترق باللعنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's continued imprisonment teaches that causes have no effect independently of God; بضع means three through nine, and the reported term here was seven years.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة البضع من الثلاث إلى التسع , والمروي هنا أنه كان سبعا

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah account says Midianites brought Joseph to Egypt and Potiphar bought him; God prospered his work, and Potiphar trusted him with his household and possessions.
rows.anchor: فأهبط المدينيون يوسف إلى مصر , فاشتراه قوطيفر الأمير صاحب شرطة فرعون

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: In the Torah account, Joseph refuses his master's wife as betrayal and sin before God, flees when she seizes his tunic, and she falsely accuses him of attempted assault.
rows.anchor: فكيف أرتكب هذا الشر العظيم

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah says Potiphar imprisoned Joseph, but God won him favor with the jailer, who entrusted him with the prisoners; whatever Joseph did prospered.
rows.anchor: فمكث هناك في السجن , وكان الرب يبصره

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The Torah says Pharaoh jailed his cupbearer and baker in Joseph's prison after they offended him, and Joseph served them; they had separate dreams on the same night.
rows.anchor: في الحبس الذي كان فيه يوسفن فسلط صاحب السجن يوسف عليهما

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: In the cupbearer's dream, a vine had three branches that budded, flowered, and ripened into grapes; he squeezed them into Pharaoh's cup and served the king.
rows.anchor: فبينا هي كذلك إذ فرعت وبنت ورقها

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: Joseph interprets the three branches as three days, after which Pharaoh will restore the cupbearer; he asks him to remember Joseph and help free him.
rows.anchor: الثلاثة قضبان هي ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: The baker dreams of three baskets of bread on his head, with birds eating the uppermost food; Joseph interprets the baskets as three days before the baker is executed and eaten by birds.
rows.anchor: ثلاثة أطباق هي ثلاثة أيام

rows.speaker: التوراة
rows.claim: On Pharaoh's birthday, the cupbearer was restored and the baker executed as Joseph predicted, but the cupbearer did not remember Joseph.
rows.anchor: فأمر برد رئيس أصحاب الشراب على موضعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the forgotten request failed, God produced another cause for Joseph's elevation; the king is a powerful ruler responsible for politics and administration.
rows.anchor: أثار الله سبحانه سببا ينفذ به ما أراد من رئاسته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king presents his vision to a court of elites, including sorcerers, priests, soothsayers, physiognomists, and sages, emphasizing that he is serious rather than testing them.
rows.anchor: وهم السحرة والكهنة والحزرة والقافة والحكماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense أرى narrates the vision as if unfolding now because it deeply alarmed the king; fat means bodily increase and عجاف means dry, emaciated thinness.
rows.anchor: حكاية للحال لشدة ما هاله من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dry ears overcome the green ears; the author says the number modifies a plural of paucity because the dream signifies famine and hardship, unlike the multiplied crop in 2:261.
rows.anchor: ولما كان تأويل المنام الجدب والقحط والشدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A سنبلة is a reed-like plant bearing an ordered cluster of grains; the repeated seven is omitted from the second ears because the lean cattle already suggest it.
rows.anchor: نبات كالقصبة حملة حبوب منتظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The king calls his leading nobles to give a precise, generous interpretation, restricting them to his dream and warning them not to speak outside their knowledge.
rows.anchor: أي الأشراف النبلاء الذين تملأ العيون مناظرهم والقلوب مخابرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿbir means crossing from the dream's outward form to its inner meaning, while taʾwil names its outcome; the root family centers on transition from one place or state to another.
rows.anchor: تأويلها بالعبور من علنها إلى سرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author extends the root ʿ-r-b across words for Friday, a loving or defiant wife, Arab vigor, swelling, abundant water, eating, and activity, relating them to characteristic movement or intensity.
rows.anchor: لعلو قدرها عن بقية الأيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other derivatives describe nomadic life, Arab identity, fluency, and escaping foreignness or ignorance; the author repeatedly explains them as moving from one state to another.
rows.anchor: أقام بالبادية , مع الأعراب الذين لا يوطنون مكانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿrīb can mean refining speech, removing error, improving a palm, or making explicit a sexual act; the author links these senses to changing or correcting a state.
rows.anchor: والتعريب : تهذيب المنطق من اللحن - كأنه رفع نفسه إلى العرب , وقطع سعف النخل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage continues the root's many senses, including removing vulgar speech, rejecting it, marriage, drinking clear water, and choosing an Arab horse, all treated as shifts in state or quality.
rows.anchor: وهما أيضا الرد عن القبيح , وذلك إدخاله في خصال العرب التي هي معالي الأخلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root ʿ-b-r covers crossing from one bank to another, a crossing place or ferry, passing away, tears, wonder, abundance, crowded gatherings, an uncherished woman, and strong travel camels.
rows.anchor: قطعته من عبره - أي شطه - إلى عبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It also means speaking for someone, weighing without exactness, a passerby, the star al-Shiʿra al-ʿAbur, a year-old sheep, and a boy nearing maturity; the examples emphasize passage or transition.
rows.anchor: فتكلمت عنه - كأنك عبرت من خاطره إلى خاطر المخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further uses include hardship, a camel that has not given birth for three years, perfume and saffron whose scent or color passes, river-grown lote, thick hair, feathered arrows, grieving, fast clouds, and strong eagles.
rows.anchor: ضرب من الطيب - لعبور ريحه , والزعفران - لعبور لونه وريحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author includes a plant called falsehood because it quickly disappears, continuing the root's association with crossing away or shifting states.
rows.anchor: الكذب والباطل - لسرعة زواله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The related root r-ʿ-b includes frightening someone, a flood filling a valley, a messenger-carrying pigeon, raising the voice, cutting a hump, a beautifully formed woman, and short stature.
rows.anchor: فهو مرعوب - لأنك أجزته من الأمن إلى الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The entry b-ʿ-r defines droppings of camels and cloven-hoofed animals, while a baʿīr can mean a camel or any load-bearing animal.
rows.anchor: رجيع الخف والظلف إلا البقر الأهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root r-b-ʿ covers home and dwelling, staying or waiting, fertility and spring, returning to one's former state, counting four, lifting loads, and tools for carrying them.
rows.anchor: المنزل والدار بعينها , والمحلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other r-b-ʿ derivatives mean weak or short, raising a stone, relieving a burden, carrying a long hump, and the spring months and seasons; the passage associates these with change, lifting, or settlement.
rows.anchor: وربع الحجر : رفعه , والحمل : رفعه على الدابة
